q: Rate limiter 的核心职责是什么？
q_en: What is the core job of a rate limiter?
text: Rate limiter 在一个时间范围内限制客户端请求数；超过阈值后会 {{throttle 或 reject}} 多余流量。
text_en: A rate limiter caps requests in a time range and {{throttles or rejects}} traffic above the limit.
why: 我会把它放在服务入口附近，先挡住超过配额的请求，再让后端处理正常流量。
why_en: A rate limiter protects backend capacity by blocking or slowing requests after a configured quota is exceeded.

q: Rate limiter 主要挡住哪些系统风险？
q_en: Which system risks does a rate limiter primarily reduce?
options: 误配置或重试风暴耗尽后端资源
多租户里某个客户长期吃掉全部配额
云成本因失控调用持续上涨
把数据库查询自动改写成索引查询
options_en: A retry storm or bad config exhausting backend resources
One tenant consuming the shared quota for a long time
Runaway calls driving cloud cost upward
Automatically rewriting database queries to use indexes
why: 它控制入口流量和公平性，也能限制失控调用的成本；但它不替数据库优化查询计划。
why_en: Rate limiting protects capacity, fairness, and cost, but it does not optimize database queries for you.
optionExplanations: 限流能在入口挡住重试风暴或误配置流量，避免它们把后端连接池和线程打满。
按客户设配额能防止某个租户长期占满共享容量，把资源公平分给其他客户。
限制失控调用次数能直接压低按请求计费的云账单，不用等到告警才处理。
查询计划优化属于数据库层的工作，限流器只控制请求量，不会帮你重写或加索引。
optionExplanations_en: It sits at the edge and stops retry storms or misconfigured traffic before they saturate backend connection pools or threads.
Per-customer quotas keep one tenant from hogging the shared capacity, so the pool stays fair for everyone else.
Capping runaway calls directly caps pay-per-request cloud spend instead of waiting for a billing alert.
Query-plan tuning is a database job; a rate limiter only caps request volume, it never rewrites or indexes your queries.

scenario: 一个公共 API 要按客户套餐限制请求数，限制值会调整，超限时客户端要得到明确反馈。
scenario_en: A public API enforces plan-based quotas, limits can change, and clients need explicit feedback when they exceed them.
q: Rate limiter 的功能需求应优先覆盖哪一组？
q_en: Which functional requirements matter most for this rate limiter?
options: 只统计全站总 QPS，不区分客户
限制时间窗口内的请求数、支持配置、超限通知
把所有请求写入队列后慢慢处理
只在客户端 SDK 里做本地计数
options_en: Only count total site QPS without client identity
Limit requests per window, make limits configurable, and notify on overflow
Put every request into a queue and process it later
Count locally only inside the client SDK
why: 题目要按套餐改配额并给反馈，所以规则配置、窗口计数和超限响应是主线。
why_en: Because quotas change by plan, the design needs configurable windowed counting and a clear over-limit response.
whenOtherWins: 如果只是保护一个内部批处理 worker，全局队列限速可能比逐客户 API 配额更合适。
tradeoff: 逐客户配额控制 vs 全局流量整形
optionExplanations: 只看全站总量分不清哪个客户超了套餐，没法按客户执行配额或调整限制。
窗口计数、可配置规则和超限通知正好覆盖套餐调整和明确反馈这两个要求。
把请求全部塞进队列会拖慢正常流量，也没法立刻告诉客户端它超限了。
只在客户端计数很容易被绕过或被清空本地状态，不能作为真正的配额执行点。
optionExplanations_en: Counting only total site QPS cannot tell which customer is over their plan, so per-customer quotas cannot be enforced.
Windowed counting, configurable rules, and overflow notification cover both requirements: adjustable plans and clear feedback.
Queuing every request slows down normal traffic and never tells the caller they went over the limit.
Client-side-only counting is easy to bypass or reset, so it cannot be the real enforcement point for quotas.

scenario: 短信服务的免费套餐每天只能发 500 条，但产品允许偶尔超出 5% 以减少误伤。
scenario_en: A messaging service caps a free plan at 500 messages per day but allows an occasional 5% buffer to reduce false blocking.
q: 这种限流策略更像哪一种 throttling？
q_en: Which throttling mode best matches this policy?
options: Hard throttling
Soft throttling
Elastic throttling
Client-side throttling
options_en: Hard throttling
Soft throttling
Elastic throttling
Client-side throttling
why: Soft throttling 允许在固定额度上加一个小缓冲；hard 会到线就拒绝，elastic 则看资源空闲程度。
why_en: Soft throttling allows a small buffer above the nominal quota instead of rejecting exactly at the limit.
whenOtherWins: 如果超一条就会造成账单或合规问题，hard throttling 更合适。
tradeoff: 严格保护配额 vs 减少边界误伤

termDefinitions.meaning: throttling：对请求放慢、排队或拒绝，避免后端被突发流量压垮。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Throttling slows, queues, or rejects requests so backend capacity is not overwhelmed.

optionExplanations: 账务或合规必须卡死上限、一条都不能超时，hard throttling 到线立即拒绝最合适。
固定额度上允许一点小幅越界，用户体验优先于绝对精确时，soft throttling 正好对应 500 条加 5% 缓冲。
后端容量会随负载波动、且能被实时观测时，elastic throttling 才谈得上按空闲资源动态放行。
客户端限流只能提示、容易被绕过，只适合可信客户端做本地节流的辅助场景。
optionExplanations_en: When a hard billing or compliance line cannot be crossed even once, hard throttling that rejects right at the limit is the fit.
When user experience matters more than exact precision, soft throttling's small buffer above a fixed quota matches 500-plus-5%.
Elastic throttling only makes sense when backend capacity is observable and actually fluctuates, letting it admit more when idle.
Client-side throttling only advises and is easy to bypass, so it fits trusted clients doing local pacing, not the main control.

scenario: 一个公网 API 的所有流量都经过统一入口，客户端不可信，后端应用服务器希望少接触无效请求。
scenario_en: All public API traffic passes through one edge layer, clients are untrusted, and app servers should avoid wasted work.
q: Rate limiter 更适合放在哪里？
q_en: Where should the rate limiter sit?
options: 只放客户端 SDK
放在入口 middleware
分散放业务函数
只在数据库触发器
options_en: Only in the client SDK
At the edge middleware
Spread across business functions
Only in database triggers
why: 统一入口能看到全量请求，也能在业务服务器前拒绝超限流量；客户端限流只能做提示，不能防绕过。
why_en: The gateway sees all traffic and can reject excess requests before expensive application work starts.
whenOtherWins: 如果是移动端离线功能，客户端本地节流可作为省电和用户体验优化。
tradeoff: 入口集中控制 vs 客户端低成本提示
diagram:
flowchart LR
  C[Client] --> G[Gateway rate limiter]
  G -->|allowed| A[API servers]
  G -->|429| R[Reject]
optionExplanations: 只信客户端 SDK 计数，等于让不可信调用方自己判断是否超限，攻击者绕过后台没有第二道防线。
所有流量都过同一入口时，网关能看到全量请求并在业务服务器动手前挡掉超限流量。
规则散在各业务函数里，只有当限流逻辑高度业务化、需要贴近具体接口时才值得作为补充。
写库时才拦截等于让应用已经把资源都花掉了，只适合保护数据库这最后一层写入。
optionExplanations_en: Trusting only the client SDK to count means the untrusted caller judges its own limit, so an attacker can just skip that code.
When all traffic passes one edge, the gateway sees every request and rejects excess before the app servers do any work.
Scattering the rule across business functions only earns its keep when the logic is deeply route-specific and needs local context.
Catching it at the database write means the app already spent its resources, so it only protects that last write layer.

scenario: 多个限流节点同时处理同一个客户的请求，产品要求超限尽量精确，但入口延迟也要低。
scenario_en: Several limiter nodes process requests from the same customer; the product wants accurate limits with low edge latency.
q: 集中式计数和分布式计数的关键取舍是什么？
q_en: What is the main tradeoff between centralized and distributed counters?
options: 集中式更精确但增加共享存储延迟和争用
分布式一定比集中式更精确
集中式完全不需要原子操作
分布式计数不能按用户限流
options_en: Centralized counters are more accurate but add shared-store latency and contention
Distributed counters are always more accurate
Centralized counters never need atomic operations
Distributed counters cannot rate-limit per user
why: 共享计数器让所有节点看到同一份状态，但每次判定要碰共享存储；本地或分布式状态更快，却会有短暂超发。
why_en: A shared counter improves accuracy but puts shared storage on the hot path, while local counters trade precision for speed.
whenOtherWins: 如果超几次请求没关系，分布式近似计数能换来更低延迟和更高可用性。
tradeoff: 计数精度 vs 判定延迟

termDefinitions.meaning: Sticky sessions：负载均衡把同一客户端固定路由到同一节点。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Sticky sessions route the same client to the same backend node.

optionExplanations: 所有节点读写同一份计数确实更准，但每次判定都要打共享存储，延迟和争用也跟着涨。
分布式计数为了低延迟牺牲了精度，不能说它一定比集中式更准，这是反过来的说法。
共享计数器仍需 INCR 或事务这类原子操作，否则并发读写会互相覆盖，不是完全不需要。
分布式计数一样能按用户 key 分片，只是精度打了折扣，不等于它不能做 per-user 限流。
optionExplanations_en: All nodes reading and writing one counter is more accurate, but every decision now hits shared storage, adding latency and contention.
Distributed counters trade precision for lower latency, so claiming they are always more accurate has it backwards.
A shared counter still needs an atomic op like INCR or a transaction, or concurrent writers overwrite each other — it is not lock-free by nature.
Distributed counters can still key by user, they just admit a bit more slack, so per-user limiting is not impossible.
diagram:
flowchart LR
  subgraph Centralized
    A1[Node A] -->|INCR key| S[(Shared counter)]
    A2[Node B] -->|INCR key| S
  end
  subgraph Distributed
    B1[Node A] --> L1[(Local counter)]
    B2[Node B] --> L2[(Local counter)]
    L1 -.periodic sync.-> L2
  end

scenario: 搜索 API 既要保护全站容量，又要让每个客户不能超过自己的套餐额度。
scenario_en: A search API must protect total service capacity while also enforcing each customer's plan quota.
q: 计数 key 应如何建模？
q_en: How should the counter keys be modeled?
options: 只统计一个全局 counter
只按机器名字分别计数
全局 + per-user counters
每次请求都用随机 counter
options_en: Count with only one global counter
Count only by server machine name
Global plus per-user counters
Every request gets its own random counter
why: 全局 counter 保护整体容量，per-user counter 才能执行套餐公平性；两条规则服务不同不变量。
why_en: A global counter protects service capacity, while per-user counters enforce fairness across customers.
whenOtherWins: 如果系统只需要挡全站雪崩，不关心租户公平性，一个全局限制就够。
tradeoff: 整体容量保护 vs 单用户公平性
optionExplanations: 只留全局 counter 能护住整体容量，但分不清哪个客户超了自己的套餐额度。
按机器名计数会随请求落到哪台机器而变化，同一个客户可能被算成好几份配额。
全局那层挡的是站点级雪崩，按用户单独开一份计数才管得住每个客户自己的套餐上限，两者各守一条不变量。
每请求随机生成 counter 等于每次都当成新客户，配额和历史请求完全对不上。
optionExplanations_en: A global-only counter protects overall capacity but cannot tell which customer went over their own plan.
Counting by server name shifts with whichever machine handled the request, so one customer's traffic gets split into several counts.
The global layer blocks a site-wide avalanche, while a separate per-user count is what actually caps each customer's own plan limit — two counters, two different invariants.
A random counter per request treats every call as a brand-new customer, so quotas never line up with real request history.

q: 限流规则为什么要缓存到内存？
q_en: Why cache rate-limit rules in memory?
text: Rule database 存服务 owner 配置，后台 retriever 监听变化并更新 {{throttle rules cache}}，让请求路径不用每次查规则库。
text_en: The rule database stores owner-defined limits, and a retriever updates the {{throttle rules cache}} so the request path avoids a database read.
why: 限流判定在每个请求上执行，规则查库会把控制面延迟放进数据面。
why_en: Because every request needs a decision, rule reads should be cached off the hot path.

q: Rate limiter 一次请求的组件链路应如何排序？
q_en: What is the component order for a rate-limiter request?
steps: Decision-maker 用规则和计数运行算法
Client identifier builder 提取 IP 或登录 ID
允许的请求进入 request processor
超限请求返回 429 或进入延后队列
Throttle rules cache 提供当前规则
why: 我会先识别是谁，再读规则和状态做判定；判定结果才决定放行、拒绝或排队。
why_en: The limiter first identifies the client, then evaluates cached rules and counters before forwarding or rejecting the request.

q: Rate limiter 的高层请求流程是什么？
q_en: What is the high-level request flow through a rate limiter?
steps: Client 发送请求到入口层
Decision-maker 判断是否在限制内
Identifier builder 生成限流 key
允许则转发给 API server
超限则返回 429 或排队
why: 这个顺序把身份、规则判断和后端执行分开，后端只处理已经通过配额检查的请求。
why_en: This flow separates identity, quota evaluation, and backend work so rejected traffic stops early.
diagram:
sequenceDiagram
  participant C as Client
  participant R as RateLimiter
  participant A as API
  C->>R: request
  R->>R: build key + check rule
  alt allowed
    R->>A: forward
  else over limit
    R-->>C: 429 Too Many Requests
  end

scenario: 某 API 超过用户配额时不应继续消耗后端资源，客户端也要知道稍后重试。
scenario_en: When a user exceeds an API quota, backend work should stop and the client should know to retry later.
q: 超限响应最合适是什么？
q_en: What is the best over-limit response?
options: 继续转发并只写日志
返回 429
返回 200 但丢响应体
改走数据库读副本
options_en: Forward it and only log the event
Return 429
Return 200 but drop the body
Route it to a database replica
why: 429 明确告诉客户端这是限流，不会伪装成成功，也不会让后端继续做无效工作。
why_en: HTTP 429 clearly communicates rate limiting and avoids doing backend work for an over-quota request.
whenOtherWins: 如果限制来自临时过载且业务允许延迟处理，把请求排队可能比直接拒绝更好。
tradeoff: 快速失败反馈 vs 延迟处理体验

termDefinitions.meaning: HTTP：客户端和服务端交换 Web 请求与响应的协议。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: HTTP is the protocol used for web requests and responses.

optionExplanations: 继续转发只写日志等于放行了超限请求，后端照样要花资源处理它，限流形同虚设。
拒绝时用标准的 429 状态码，客户端立刻能分辨这不是业务成功，后端也不再浪费资源处理这条请求。
返回 200 但丢响应体会让客户端误以为请求成功，实际却拿不到任何数据。
改走数据库读副本解决的是读扩展问题，跟拒绝超限请求完全是两件事。
optionExplanations_en: Forwarding it and only logging still lets the over-limit request cost backend work, so the limiter accomplishes nothing.
A 429 tells the client plainly that this was rate-limited, without spending backend work or pretending the call succeeded.
Returning 200 with an empty body makes the client think it succeeded while it actually got nothing back.
Routing to a database read replica solves read scaling, which is a different problem from rejecting an over-quota request.

scenario: 两个限流节点几乎同时读取同一个用户 counter=4，limit=5，然后都决定允许并写回。
scenario_en: Two limiter nodes read the same user's counter as 4 with limit 5, both allow the request, and then write back.
q: 普通 read-modify-write 会带来什么问题？
q_en: What problem can plain read-modify-write cause here?
options: 并发允许却丢一次计数
请求会被永久拒绝
规则缓存自动修复
LB 自动串行请求
options_en: Both allow but one increment is lost
Requests are rejected forever
The rule cache fixes it automatically
The load balancer serializes requests
why: 两个节点都读到旧值 4，都判断 4 < 5 所以放行；然后各自计算 4+1=5 并写回 5。真实发生了 2 个请求，但 counter 最后还是 5，只增加了 1 次，系统低估流量，下一次可能继续误放行。
why_en: Both nodes read the old value 4, both see 4 < 5 and allow, then both compute 4+1=5 and write 5 back. Two requests happened, but the counter only increased once, so the limiter undercounts and may allow too much traffic.

termDefinitions.meaning: 先读旧值，在应用里计算新值，再写回；如果读和写不是一个原子动作，并发时可能互相覆盖。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Read-modify-write reads an old value, computes a new value in the app, then writes it back; if the cycle is not atomic, concurrent writers can overwrite each other.

termDefinitions.meaning: 两次并发更新都发生了，但其中一次更新效果被另一次写回覆盖，最终状态只反映一次。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A lost update happens when two concurrent updates both occur, but one effect is overwritten so the final state reflects only one update.

termDefinitions.meaning: Redis 原子自增命令，把读、加一、写回合成服务端一个不可被插队的操作。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: INCR is Redis's atomic increment command, combining read, add-one, and write-back into one server-side operation.

optionExplanations: 两个节点各自读到旧值再写回，结果 counter 只从 4 变成 5，两次放行却只记了一次，这正是 lost update。
这里不是永久拒绝，问题恰恰相反：系统会因为计数偏低而继续误放行更多请求。
规则缓存只存配置这类静态数据，修不了并发读写计数器时产生的竞态问题。
普通负载均衡不会自动把同一用户的请求串行化，除非显式做 sticky routing 或单队列。
optionExplanations_en: Each node reads the old value and writes its own +1, so the counter only moves from 4 to 5 despite two admits — that's a lost update.
This is not permanent rejection; if anything the opposite happens, since undercounting lets more requests slip through later.
A rule cache only holds static config, so it cannot fix a race that happens when two writers update a counter concurrently.
A normal load balancer doesn't serialize one user's requests on its own unless you add sticky routing or a single queue.

scenario: 限流节点共享 Redis counter，希望一次操作完成自增并拿到新值，避免 read-modify-write 丢更新。
scenario_en: Limiter nodes share a Redis counter and need one operation that increments and returns the new value.
q: 哪种 Redis 操作最适合做基础 counter 更新？
q_en: Which Redis operation best fits a basic counter update?
options: GET 后在应用里 +1 再 SET
INCR key
LRANGE key 0 -1
KEYS *
options_en: GET, add one in the app, then SET
INCR key
LRANGE key 0 -1
KEYS *
why: INCR 把加一和返回新值放在 Redis 的原子操作里，避免多个节点覆盖同一个旧值。
why_en: INCR performs the increment atomically inside Redis, avoiding lost updates from app-side read-modify-write.
whenOtherWins: 如果要同时检查 limit、设置 TTL、返回剩余额度，Lua 脚本比单条 INCR 更完整。
tradeoff: 单命令原子性 vs 多步骤策略表达
codeSample:
INCR rl:user:42
EXPIRE rl:user:42 60
# 简单窗口计数；生产中要处理 EXPIRE 与 INCR 的组合原子性。

termDefinitions.meaning: Redis：常用的内存键值存储，支持原子计数等低延迟操作。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Redis is an in-memory key-value store often used for low-latency atomic counters.

termDefinitions.meaning: TTL：键或缓存项在自动过期前可存活的时间。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: TTL is the time a key or cached item remains valid before expiring.

optionExplanations: GET 后在应用里加一再 SET 拆成三步，节点之间可能读到同一个旧值，写回时互相覆盖。
INCR 把读旧值、加一、写回压成 Redis 内部一次原子操作，多个节点不会互相踩计数。
LRANGE 是取列表区间的命令，跟维护一个自增计数器完全是两回事，用不上。
KEYS * 会扫描整个 keyspace 阻塞 Redis，既不是计数命令，生产环境也该避免。
optionExplanations_en: GET, add one in the app, then SET splits the update into three steps, so nodes can read the same old value and overwrite each other.
INCR folds read, increment, and write-back into one atomic op inside Redis, so concurrent nodes never step on the same count.
LRANGE reads a range from a list, which has nothing to do with maintaining a simple increment counter.
KEYS * scans the whole keyspace and blocks Redis; it isn't a counting command and should be avoided in production.

scenario: 固定窗口限流要在 Redis 里一次完成：读当前计数、判断 limit、允许时自增并设置过期时间。
scenario_en: A fixed-window limiter needs Redis to check the current count, compare the limit, increment on allow, and set expiry in one atomic step.
q: 为什么用 Lua 脚本比多条客户端命令更稳？
q_en: Why is a Lua script safer than several client-side Redis commands?
options: Lua 可以把检查、递增和过期绑定成一次原子执行
Lua 会让 Redis 自动跨机房强一致
Lua 能保证请求永远不被拒绝
Lua 会替代所有限流算法
options_en: Lua can bind check, increment, and expiry into one atomic execution
Lua makes Redis strongly consistent across regions automatically
Lua guarantees requests are never rejected
Lua replaces every rate-limiting algorithm
why: 多条命令之间可能被别的请求插入；Lua 在 Redis 内部一次跑完，窗口计数不会漏掉中间状态。
why_en: A Redis Lua script avoids interleaving between separate commands by running the check and update atomically.
whenOtherWins: 如果只是单机低 QPS 的演示，INCR 加过期处理已经够简单。
tradeoff: 原子策略执行 vs 脚本复杂度
codeSample:
local c = tonumber(redis.call('GET', KEYS[1]) or '0')
if c >= tonumber(ARGV[1]) then return 0 end
c = redis.call('INCR', KEYS[1])
if c == 1 then redis.call('EXPIRE', KEYS[1], ARGV[2]) end
return 1

termDefinitions.meaning: Lua：Redis 支持的脚本语言，可把多条命令作为一次脚本执行。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Lua is the scripting language Redis can execute to combine multiple commands atomically.

termDefinitions.meaning: Redis：常用的内存键值存储，支持脚本和原子计数。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Redis is an in-memory key-value store that supports scripts and atomic counters.

optionExplanations: Lua 脚本把检查、递增和设置过期打包成 Redis 端一次原子执行，别的请求没办法插进两条命令中间。
Lua 只保证单个 Redis 节点内脚本原子执行，不会让跨地域复制自动变成强一致。
限流的目的就是要拒绝超额请求，Lua 只是让判定更准，并不会让请求永远通过。
Lua 只是把多条命令捆成一次执行的手段，具体用哪种限流算法仍要另外选。
optionExplanations_en: A Lua script runs the check, increment, and expiry inside Redis in one shot, so no other request can slip in between steps.
Lua only guarantees atomic execution on a single Redis node — it doesn't turn cross-region replication into strong consistency.
The whole point of rate limiting is to reject excess traffic; Lua just makes that decision atomic, it doesn't guarantee admission.
Lua is just a way to bundle several commands into one execution; you still have to pick which limiting algorithm to run.

scenario: 一个热门 API key 每秒有大量请求，单个 Redis counter 成为写热点，但限流读可以接受多读几个 key。
scenario_en: A hot API key receives many requests per second; one Redis counter is a write hotspot, but reads can tolerate summing several keys.
q: 如何降低 counter 写争用？
q_en: How can you reduce write contention on the counter?
options: counter 分片，读时求和
全局锁包住单个 counter
固定到一台机器计数
只靠离线日志统计
options_en: Shard the counter and sum on read
Wrap one counter with a global lock
Pin counting to one machine
Count only from offline logs
why: 分片把写压力摊到多个 key 上；代价是判定时要读多个 shard 求和，读路径会更重。
why_en: Sharded counters spread writes across keys, trading lower write contention for a heavier read path.
whenOtherWins: 如果请求量低且精确性强，单个原子 counter 更简单。
tradeoff: 写入争用 vs 读取求和成本
optionExplanations: 热点写入很集中时，把 counter 拆成多个 key 分片能把写压力摊开，代价是判定要读多个 shard 求和。
全局锁把所有更新排成一条队，争用只会更严重，只有并发很低时锁的开销才可以接受。
把计数固定到一台机器能避开锁，但机器故障会直接影响这个用户的限流判定，牺牲了容错。
只靠离线日志统计意味着限流决策滞后到事后分析，没法在请求到达时实时拒绝超限流量。
optionExplanations_en: When one key is a hot write target, sharding the counter across several keys spreads the writes, at the cost of summing shards to read.
A global lock serializes every update onto one queue, which only makes contention worse; it's fine only when concurrency is already low.
Pinning counting to one machine dodges locking, but a failure on that machine directly breaks limiting for that user — you traded away fault tolerance.
Counting only from offline logs pushes the decision to after-the-fact analysis, so it can't reject an over-limit request as it arrives.

scenario: 为了降低入口延迟，限流服务先按缓存计数放行，再异步更新真实 counter。
scenario_en: To reduce edge latency, the limiter allows based on cached counts and updates the real counter asynchronously.
q: 这种优化的主要代价是什么？
q_en: What is the main cost of this optimization?
options: 可能短时间放过少量超额请求
所有请求都会变成强一致事务
规则配置无法再更新
客户端必须改用 UDP
options_en: A few over-limit requests may slip through briefly
All requests become strongly consistent transactions
Rules can no longer be updated
Clients must switch to UDP
why: 把更新移出关键路径能降延迟，但判定看到的是旧计数，所以会用精度换吞吐。
why_en: Moving updates off the hot path lowers latency but lets decisions use slightly stale counts.

termDefinitions.meaning: UDP：无连接传输协议，不保证重传或顺序。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: UDP is a connectionless transport protocol that does not guarantee delivery or ordering.

optionExplanations: 判定用的是稍微滞后的缓存计数，异步写回追上真实值之前，确实可能多放行几个请求。
这个优化恰恰是为了避免同步事务的延迟，说它变成强一致事务正好说反了。
规则缓存和计数更新是两回事，retriever 仍能正常刷新规则，规则并没有被锁死。
限流是否异步更新 counter 跟客户端用什么传输协议无关，UDP 不是这里的变量。
optionExplanations_en: The decision uses a slightly stale cached count, so before the async write-back catches up a few extra requests can slip through.
This optimization exists specifically to avoid synchronous-transaction latency, so calling it strongly consistent is backwards.
Rule caching and counter updates are separate concerns; the retriever still refreshes rules normally, nothing gets locked.
Whether counter updates are async has nothing to do with which transport protocol clients use — UDP isn't a variable here.

scenario: 限流存储短暂不可用。支付防刷接口宁可误拒，也不能让攻击流量无限进入；普通图片浏览接口更怕整体不可用。
scenario_en: The limiter store is briefly unavailable. A payment anti-abuse endpoint would rather reject than let attacks through, while image browsing fears global outage.
q: fail-open 和 fail-closed 应如何选择？
q_en: How should you choose between fail-open and fail-closed?
options: 按风险分开选
所有接口 fail-closed
所有接口 fail-open
失败时删掉规则
options_en: Choose by endpoint risk
Fail closed for every endpoint
Fail open for every endpoint
Delete rules on failure
why: 安全和成本边界硬的接口更适合失败即拒绝；可用性优先的读接口可以临时放行并告警。
why_en: Security-critical endpoints should fail closed, while availability-first reads can fail open with monitoring.
whenOtherWins: 如果浏览接口也在被大规模攻击，临时 fail-closed 或降级页会更安全。
tradeoff: 安全边界 vs 服务可用性
optionExplanations: 支付这类硬边界接口失败就该拒绝，图片浏览这类可用性优先接口可以临时放行并告警，按风险分策略两边都顾到。
所有接口都 fail-closed 意味着图片浏览这种低风险读请求也会在存储抖动时被整体拒绝。
所有接口都 fail-open 意味着支付防刷这类高风险接口在存储故障时会放攻击流量直接穿透。
失败时删掉规则不仅不解决问题，恢复后限流规则也一起丢了，控制面状态被破坏。
optionExplanations_en: A hard-boundary endpoint like payment should fail closed, while an availability-first read can fail open with alerts — splitting by risk covers both.
Making every endpoint fail closed means low-risk reads like image browsing get rejected outright whenever storage hiccups.
Making every endpoint fail open means a high-risk endpoint like payment anti-abuse lets attack traffic straight through during an outage.
Deleting rules on failure doesn't fix anything and also wipes the control-plane state, so limits stay lost even after recovery.

q: Token bucket 如何更新 token 数？
q_en: How does a token bucket update its token count?
text: 到达请求时可用 token 通常更新为 {{min(C, oldTokens + elapsed * R)}}；请求消耗 N 个 token，不足则拒绝或只处理可用部分。
text_en: On arrival, tokens are often updated as {{min(C, oldTokens + elapsed * R)}}; a request consumes N tokens and is rejected if insufficient.
why: C 控制最大突发，R 控制长期速率；这个公式把突发容量和平均限速分开调。
why_en: Capacity controls burst size, while refill rate controls the long-term request rate.

scenario: 一个 API 允许用户短时间连点几次，但长期平均不能超过每秒 10 次。
scenario_en: An API should allow short bursts of clicks but keep the long-term average below 10 requests per second.
q: 哪种算法最贴合这个需求？
q_en: Which algorithm best fits this requirement?
options: Token bucket
Leaking bucket
Fixed window counter
只按日志离线统计
options_en: Token bucket
Leaking bucket
Fixed window counter
Offline log counting only
why: Token bucket 让攒下来的 token 支持短突发，同时 refill rate 限制长期平均速率。
why_en: Token bucket supports bursts with saved tokens while the refill rate controls the long-term average.
whenOtherWins: 如果下游必须看到完全平滑的出流，leaking bucket 更合适。
tradeoff: 允许突发 vs 平滑出流
optionExplanations: 短时间连点几次要能过、长期平均又要卡在 10/s，token bucket 用攒下的 token 撑突发、refill rate 卡均速，正好两头都占。
Leaking bucket 按固定速率漏出请求，会把连点的突发也压成平滑出流，牺牲了短时爆发的体验。
Fixed window counter 只按窗口边界算数，窗口交界处容易被两侧突发叠加，达不到长期平均限速的效果。
只靠日志离线统计意味着请求已经发生完才算数，没法在真实调用时就拦住超速的那一下。
optionExplanations_en: Since short click bursts should pass but the long-run average must stay under 10/s, token bucket's saved tokens cover the burst while the refill rate caps the average — it fits both.
Leaking bucket drains at a fixed rate, which smooths out the click burst too, trading away the burst-friendly experience the requirement wants.
A fixed window counter only counts inside window boundaries, so traffic straddling the edge can stack up and blow past the intended average.
Counting only from offline logs means the tally happens after the fact, so it can't block the over-rate call as it actually arrives.

scenario: 下游服务只能稳定处理每秒 100 个任务，不希望看到任何突发尖峰。
scenario_en: A downstream service can process a steady 100 jobs per second and should not see bursts.
q: 哪种限流算法更适合平滑出流？
q_en: Which limiter best smooths outbound traffic?
options: Leaking bucket
Token bucket
Fixed window counter
随机丢弃一半请求
options_en: Leaking bucket
Token bucket
Fixed window counter
Randomly drop half the requests
why: Leaking bucket 用 FIFO 队列按固定速率漏出请求，突发会被排队或丢弃。
why_en: Leaking bucket drains a FIFO queue at a fixed rate, smoothing bursts before they hit the downstream service.
whenOtherWins: 如果希望保留用户短突发体验，token bucket 更自然。
tradeoff: 平滑出流 vs 突发体验

termDefinitions.meaning: FIFO：先进入队列的请求先被处理。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: FIFO means the first item entering a queue is processed first.

optionExplanations: 下游只能稳定处理 100/s 且怕突发尖峰，leaking bucket 靠 FIFO 队列把请求按固定速率一条条放出去，天然就是平滑出流。
Token bucket 允许攒下的 token 一次性花掉，出流会有尖峰，跟不希望看到任何突发正好相反。
Fixed window counter 按窗口重置计数，窗口边界仍可能出现两侧叠加的短时尖峰，不算平滑。
随机丢弃一半请求既不保证下游速率稳定在 100/s，也会误伤正常请求，不是有意义的整形方式。
optionExplanations_en: Since downstream can only take a steady 100/s and hates spikes, a leaking bucket drains a FIFO queue at a fixed rate — naturally smooth output.
Token bucket lets saved tokens burst out all at once, which produces exactly the spike the requirement says it doesn't want.
A fixed window counter resets at each boundary, so traffic straddling two windows can still stack into a short spike, not a smooth flow.
Randomly dropping half the requests neither guarantees a steady 100/s downstream nor spares legitimate traffic — it isn't real shaping.

scenario: 固定窗口限制每分钟 10 次，请求在 01:29 来 10 次、01:30 又来 10 次。
scenario_en: A fixed window allows 10 requests per minute; 10 arrive at 01:29 and another 10 at 01:30.
q: 固定窗口 counter 的边界问题是什么？
q_en: What boundary problem does a fixed-window counter have?
options: 短时间内可能放行接近两倍窗口额度
它必须存每个请求的时间戳
它完全不允许突发
它无法设置窗口大小
options_en: It may allow nearly two windows of traffic in a short time
It must store every request timestamp
It never allows bursts
It cannot configure window size
why: 窗口边界重置 counter，攻击者可以把请求堆在边界两侧，形成 edge burst。
why_en: The counter resets at the boundary, so traffic clustered around the edge can exceed the intended rolling rate.
optionExplanations: 01:29 用满 10 次、01:30 计数一清零又能再来 10 次，短短两分钟内实际放行了接近两倍窗口额度。
固定窗口只存一个计数值，不需要存每次请求的时间戳，这点是 sliding window log 才要做的事。
固定窗口本身允许在一个窗口内攒满配额一次性打出去，说它完全不允许突发是反的。
窗口大小完全可以配置成 1 分钟或其他值，问题出在窗口边界重置，不是配置能力。
optionExplanations_en: Using all 10 at 01:29 and getting a fresh 10 the moment 01:30 resets means nearly double the intended quota lands in two minutes.
A fixed window only keeps a single counter value; storing every request timestamp is what a sliding window log does, not this.
A fixed window actually lets you burn the whole quota in one burst within a window, so saying it never allows bursts is backwards.
The window size is fully configurable to any length; the boundary reset is the actual problem, not a lack of configuration.

scenario: 登录防爆破必须准确限制任意滚动 60 秒内的尝试次数，内存成本可以接受。
scenario_en: A login brute-force guard must accurately limit attempts in any rolling 60-second window, and memory cost is acceptable.
q: 哪种算法最准确地消除窗口边界突发？
q_en: Which algorithm most accurately removes boundary bursts?
options: Sliding window log
Fixed window counter
Token bucket
只按每小时总量计数
options_en: Sliding window log
Fixed window counter
Token bucket
Count only hourly totals
why: Sliding window log 保存每次请求时间戳，先删掉窗口外记录，再按当前 log 大小判断。
why_en: Sliding window log keeps request timestamps and evaluates the exact rolling window.
whenOtherWins: 如果内存比精度更重要，sliding window counter 或 token bucket 更合适。
tradeoff: 滚动窗口精度 vs 时间戳内存
optionExplanations: 登录防爆破要求任意滚动 60 秒内都精确，这里就该选会给每一次请求记时间戳、且能按当前留存数量做判断的那个算法，精度最高。
Fixed window counter 在整分钟边界重置，攻击者能把尝试堆在边界两侧凑出接近双倍的滚动窗口流量。
Token bucket 关注的是长期速率和突发容量，不会精确消除某个具体窗口边界的突发问题。
只按每小时总量计数根本看不到 60 秒级别的滚动窗口，防不住短时间内的密集爆破尝试。
optionExplanations_en: Since brute-force guarding needs accuracy in any rolling 60-second window, a sliding window log stores every timestamp, prunes stale ones, then judges by log size — the most precise option.
A fixed window counter resets at minute boundaries, so an attacker can straddle the edge and push close to double the intended rolling rate.
Token bucket is tuned for long-run rate and burst capacity; it doesn't specifically eliminate a boundary spike in one window.
Counting only hourly totals can't see a 60-second rolling window at all, so it misses a dense burst of login attempts.

q: Sliding window counter 的估算公式表达了什么？
q_en: What does the sliding-window-counter formula express?
text: Hybrid counter 用 {{previousCount * remainingWindowFraction + currentCount}} 估算滚动窗口内请求量。
text_en: The hybrid counter estimates rolling-window traffic as {{previousCount * remainingWindowFraction + currentCount}}.
why: 它不用保存每个时间戳，用上一窗口的加权部分平滑边界；代价是假设上一窗口请求分布比较均匀。
why_en: It avoids per-request timestamps by weighting the previous window, but it assumes previous traffic was roughly even.

scenario: 你要给面试官快速比较五种限流算法，重点是内存成本和是否允许突发。
scenario_en: You need to compare five rate-limiting algorithms by memory cost and burst behavior.
q: 哪种算法的内存成本最高？
q_en: Which algorithm has the highest memory cost?
options: Sliding window log
Token bucket
Leaking bucket
Fixed window counter
options_en: Sliding window log
Token bucket
Leaking bucket
Fixed window counter
why: Sliding window log 要存窗口内每次请求的时间戳，其他几个通常只存少量计数或桶状态。
why_en: Sliding window log stores one timestamp per request, while the others usually keep only compact counter or bucket state.
whenOtherWins: 如果内存很紧且能接受近似，sliding window counter 是更轻的折中。
tradeoff: 精确滚动窗口 vs 内存占用
optionExplanations: 该算法给窗口内每一次到达的请求都单独记一个时间戳，请求越多占用越大，内存随请求量线性往上涨。
Token bucket 只存容量和 refill rate 这几个小参数，允许突发但状态本身很轻。
Leaking bucket 只需要维护一个 FIFO 队列和固定出流速率，状态小但突发会被排队而不是立刻放行。
Fixed window counter 每个窗口只存一个数字，状态最小，代价是边界处会出现突发。
optionExplanations_en: A sliding window log stores one timestamp per request inside the window, so memory grows linearly with request volume.
Token bucket only keeps a couple of small numbers — capacity and refill rate — so it allows bursts while staying light on state.
Leaking bucket only needs a FIFO queue and a fixed drain rate; its state is small, but bursts get queued instead of admitted immediately.
A fixed window counter keeps just one number per window, the smallest footprint, at the cost of edge bursts.

scenario: counter 并发低时锁开销可以接受；并发高时同一个 counter 上的锁让请求排队。
scenario_en: Locks may be fine at low counter contention, but high contention makes requests queue on the same counter.
q: 锁、原子操作和分片 counter 的关系应如何表述？
q_en: How should you describe locks, atomic operations, and sharded counters?
options: 低争用可用锁；高争用优先原子操作、细粒度锁或分片
锁在任何场景都一定错误
原子操作会自动解决所有热点
分片 counter 会让读取永远免费
options_en: Locks can work at low contention; high contention needs atomic ops, finer locks, or sharding
Locks are always wrong
Atomic operations automatically solve every hotspot
Sharded counters make reads free forever
why: 锁不是原罪，问题是高争用下串行化会放大延迟；分片把写散开，但读要聚合。
why_en: Locks are acceptable at low contention, but high contention needs atomicity or sharding to avoid serializing every request.
whenOtherWins: 如果只有单线程或极低 QPS，普通锁的简单性可能赢。
tradeoff: 实现简单 vs 热点争用
optionExplanations: 并发低时锁的开销可以接受，并发一高就该换成原子操作、更细粒度的锁或者分片来避免串行化放大延迟。
锁本身不是原罪，低争用场景下用锁完全没问题，说锁任何场景都错过于绝对。
原子操作解决的是单个 key 上的竞态，key 本身还是热点的话，原子操作也扛不住高并发写入。
分片能把写压力摊开，但判定时要读多个 shard 求和，读路径反而变重，不是永远免费。
optionExplanations_en: Locks are fine when contention is low, but high contention needs atomic ops, finer-grained locks, or sharding to avoid serializing every request.
Locks are not inherently wrong; at low contention they work fine, so calling them always wrong overstates the problem.
Atomic ops fix the race on one key, but if that key is still a hotspot, high write concurrency can still overwhelm it.
Sharding spreads out the writes, but reads now have to sum across shards, so the read path gets heavier, not free.

scenario: 四个选项里只有 sliding window log、fixed window counter、token bucket 和 none；题目问谁能平滑窗口边界尖峰。
scenario_en: The choices are sliding window log, fixed window counter, token bucket, and none; the question asks which smooths window-edge spikes.
q: 在这组选项中应选哪个？
q_en: Which option should you choose from this set?
options: Token bucket
Sliding window log
Fixed window counter
None of the above
options_en: Token bucket
Sliding window log
Fixed window counter
None of the above
why: Sliding window log 按真实滚动窗口检查时间戳，正好修 fixed window 的边界突发。
why_en: Sliding window log checks the real rolling window and avoids the fixed-window edge spike.
whenOtherWins: 如果选项里有 sliding window counter，它也能用近似方式平滑突发。
tradeoff: 精确时间戳 vs 近似平滑
optionExplanations: Token bucket 平滑的是长期平均速率，不是针对某个窗口边界两端拼起来才出现的短时高峰专门设计的。
这道题要挑能修 fixed window 边界高峰的算法：靠保留每次请求时间戳做真实滚动判断的那个就是它。
Fixed window counter 正是题目描述里制造出那种边界高峰的算法，选它等于把问题本身选成了答案。
能对付边界高峰的算法已经在候选里出现了，不必退回到都不对这个选项。
optionExplanations_en: Token bucket smooths the long-run average; it isn't specifically built to counter the short spike created where two windows meet.
The pick here is whichever algorithm fixes the fixed-window edge spike: the one that keeps a real timestamp per request and checks the true rolling window is it.
Fixed window counter is precisely the algorithm that produces the edge-spike behavior described, so choosing it just restates the problem.
An algorithm that already handles the edge spike is sitting among the choices, so there's no need to fall back to none of the above.

q: 设计分布式 rate limiter 时，一条合理决策链是什么？
q_en: What is a reasonable decision chain for a distributed rate limiter?
steps: 用 Redis 原子操作或 Lua 保护共享 counter
先明确每用户窗口限额和超限反馈
入口层按 client key 做判定
热点 key 用 sharded counter 降低写争用
根据业务风险选择 fail-open 或 fail-closed
why: 我会先定规则和入口，再处理并发正确性、热点扩展和故障策略。
why_en: Define the quota and edge decision first, then handle atomicity, hotspot scaling, and failure policy.

scenario: 同一个公司账号可能从多个 IP 调用 API，套餐额度应按登录账号而不是来源地址执行。
scenario_en: The same company account may call the API from many IPs, and the plan quota should apply to the logged-in account rather than source address.
q: client identifier builder 应优先使用什么 key？
q_en: Which key should the client identifier builder prefer?
options: 登录账号或 API key
当前 TCP 端口
随机 request ID
响应体大小
options_en: Logged-in account or API key
Current TCP port
Random request ID
Response body size
why: 限额绑定的是客户身份，使用随机请求或临时连接属性会把同一客户拆散，无法执行套餐配额。
why_en: The quota belongs to customer identity, so the limiter key should be account-based rather than connection-based.
whenOtherWins: 匿名接口没有登录态时，可以退而使用 IP 加设备指纹等近似 key。
tradeoff: 身份准确性 vs 匿名流量覆盖

termDefinitions.meaning: TCP：面向连接的传输协议，提供有序可靠字节流。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: TCP is a connection-oriented transport protocol that provides reliable ordered bytes.

termDefinitions.meaning: API：服务暴露给调用方使用的接口。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An API is an interface a service exposes for callers.

optionExplanations: 同一账号从多个 IP 调用时，登录账号或 API key 才是稳定跨连接不变的身份，能把这些请求合并计数。
TCP 端口是临时连接属性，每次建连都可能变化，用它做 key 会把同一客户拆成好几份。
随机 request ID 每次请求都不同，等于每次都当成新客户，历史配额完全对不上。
响应体大小是响应生成之后才知道的数据，用来做限流 key 既滞后又跟客户身份无关。
optionExplanations_en: Since the same account calls from many IPs, the logged-in account or API key is the stable identity across connections that lets counts merge.
A TCP port is a transient connection property that can change on every reconnect, so keying on it splits one customer into several buckets.
A random request ID differs on every call, effectively treating each request as a brand-new customer with no quota history.
Response body size is only known after the response is built, so it's both too late and unrelated to who the caller actually is.

scenario: 后端只是短暂过载，订单请求可以晚几秒处理，但不能无声丢失。
scenario_en: The backend is briefly overloaded; order requests can wait a few seconds but must not disappear silently.
q: Soft / elastic 限流下超额请求可以怎么处理？
q_en: How can excess requests be handled under soft or elastic limiting?
options: 进入队列等待资源恢复
直接返回成功但不执行
永久删除请求
让客户端自行猜测结果
options_en: Queue them until capacity recovers
Return success without executing
Delete the requests forever
Make the client guess the outcome
why: 可延迟的请求适合排队，系统用等待时间换成功率；但队列需要容量上限和超时。
why_en: Queueing trades latency for completion when brief overload is acceptable, but the queue still needs limits and timeouts.
whenOtherWins: 如果请求是页面浏览这类可重试读请求，直接 429 让客户端退避更简单。
tradeoff: 成功率 vs 排队延迟
optionExplanations: 订单可以晚几秒但不能丢，把超额请求放进队列等资源恢复，用等待时间换成功率。
直接返回成功却不执行会让客户端以为订单已处理，实际什么都没发生，这是无声丢失。
永久删除请求就是彻底丢单，跟不能无声丢失这条要求直接冲突。
让客户端自己猜结果既不给出明确状态，也没有真正处理请求，等于甩锅给调用方。
optionExplanations_en: Since orders can wait a few seconds but must not vanish, queueing the excess request until capacity frees up trades wait time for completion.
Returning success without executing makes the client believe the order went through when nothing actually happened — a silent loss.
Permanently deleting the request is a silent loss by definition, directly violating the must-not-disappear requirement.
Making the client guess the outcome gives no real status and never actually processes the request — it just offloads the problem.

q: Rate limiter 的非功能目标通常包括哪些？
q_en: Which non-functional goals usually matter for a rate limiter?
options: 高可用，因为它本身在保护系统入口
低延迟，因为每个请求都会经过它
可扩展，因为客户和请求会增长
强制把所有业务数据改成图数据库
options_en: High availability because it protects the system edge
Low latency because every request passes through it
Scalability because clients and requests grow
Forcing all business data into a graph database
why: 限流器在关键路径上，挂了或变慢都会影响正常流量；业务数据库模型不是它的非功能目标。
why_en: A limiter sits on the critical path, so availability, latency, and scalability are core requirements.
optionExplanations: 限流器挂了会让入口失去保护，所以高可用是硬指标，一旦不可用就等于挡不住风暴。
每个请求都要过限流判定，低延迟能防止它自己变成新的性能瓶颈拖慢正常流量。
客户和请求数会持续增长，可扩展性保证限流层能跟着业务规模一起横向扩容。
把业务数据强制改成图数据库跟限流器的职责无关，这是数据建模问题，不是它该管的事。
optionExplanations_en: If the limiter goes down, the edge loses its protection, so high availability is a hard requirement, not a nice-to-have.
Every request passes through the decision, so low latency keeps the limiter from becoming a new bottleneck for normal traffic.
Clients and request volume keep growing, so scalability lets the limiting layer scale horizontally along with the business.
Forcing business data into a graph database has nothing to do with a rate limiter's job — that's a data-modeling concern, not this one.

scenario: 负载均衡把同一客户固定路由到同一个限流节点，以便该节点本地计数更准确。
scenario_en: The load balancer pins the same customer to one limiter node so local counting is more accurate.
q: Sticky sessions 的主要代价是什么？
q_en: What is the main cost of sticky sessions?
options: 节点故障或扩容时更难均衡和迁移状态
每次请求都会自动跨区域复制
本地计数会消失所有延迟
它禁止 per-user 限流
options_en: Failures and scaling become harder because state is pinned
Every request is automatically replicated cross-region
Local counting removes all latency
It forbids per-user rate limiting
why: 固定路由让本地计数容易，但客户状态绑在节点上，故障转移和重新均衡会更麻烦。
why_en: Sticky routing simplifies local counting but makes failover and rebalancing harder because state is tied to a node.
optionExplanations: 客户状态绑在固定节点上，那个节点故障或要扩容时，状态迁移和重新均衡都变得更麻烦。
Sticky sessions 只是把同一客户固定路由到同一节点，不会自动触发跨区域数据复制。
本地计数确实更快，但延迟只是变低不是完全消失，把它说成消失所有延迟过头了。
同一节点内部依然可以按 per-user 维度继续做限流判断，粘性路由只是决定了请求送到哪个节点。
optionExplanations_en: Because customer state is pinned to one node, failing that node over or rebalancing traffic gets harder since the state has to move too.
Sticky sessions just pin one customer to one node consistently — they don't automatically trigger cross-region replication.
Local counting is faster, but it only lowers latency, not eliminates it entirely; that overstates the benefit.
Sticky sessions only decide which node handles the request; per-user limiting can still run fine inside that node.

scenario: 每个限流节点本地计数并周期性同步，系统追求低延迟，允许很小的配额误差。
scenario_en: Each limiter node counts locally and syncs periodically; the system prefers low latency and tolerates tiny quota error.
q: 这种分布式计数最可能出现什么行为？
q_en: What behavior is most likely with this distributed counting design?
options: 同步前可能短暂超出真实全局限制
所有节点都会看到完全相同的即时计数
请求必须串行经过一个锁
每个用户只能从一个城市访问
options_en: The true global limit may be exceeded briefly before sync
All nodes see the exact same instant count
Requests must pass through one serial lock
Each user can access from only one city
why: 本地快判定减少延迟，但同步有滞后；这就是用精确性换可扩展性。
why_en: Local decisions reduce latency, but delayed synchronization can allow brief overrun of the global limit.
optionExplanations: 每个节点先本地判定再周期同步，同步之前多个节点各自放行，真实全局用量短暂超出配额也不奇怪。
各节点在同步间隔之间看到的是自己的本地值，说所有节点完全相同的即时计数忽略了同步延迟。
本地计数的设计初衷正是为了避免串行锁，请求并不需要都排队经过同一把锁。
限流 key 按用户维度计数，跟用户实际访问的城市没有关系，不存在只能从一个城市访问的限制。
optionExplanations_en: Since each node decides locally and syncs periodically, several nodes can admit requests before syncing, so the true global count can briefly overshoot.
Between sync intervals every node only sees its own local value, so claiming all nodes see the exact same instant count ignores that lag.
The whole point of local counting is to avoid a serial lock, so requests don't all have to queue through one shared lock.
The limiter key is scoped to the user, not their city, so there's no rule limiting access to a single city.

rows: 多节点合并后的真实值

q: Token bucket 的关键参数有哪些？
q_en: Which parameters define a token bucket?
options: Bucket capacity C
Refill rate R
Request cost N
数据库表的列数
options_en: Bucket capacity C
Refill rate R
Request cost N
The number of columns in a database table
why: C 决定最多攒多少 token，R 决定补充速度，N 决定一次请求消耗多少。
why_en: Capacity controls saved tokens, refill rate controls replenishment, and request cost controls consumption.
optionExplanations: Bucket capacity C 定了 token 最多能攒到多少，直接决定桶能吸收多大的突发。
Refill rate R 决定 token 补充的速度，是长期平均放行速率的直接来源。
Request cost N 决定一次请求要扣多少 token，权重高的请求可以设成消耗更多。
数据库表列数属于数据建模的范畴，跟 token bucket 要维护的运行参数没有关系。
optionExplanations_en: Bucket capacity C caps how many tokens can pile up, which directly sets how big a burst the bucket can absorb.
Refill rate R sets how fast tokens replenish, which is the direct source of the long-run average admit rate.
Request cost N sets how many tokens one call spends, so a heavier request can be priced to cost more.
The number of columns in a database table is a data-modeling detail, unrelated to any runtime parameter a token bucket tracks.

q: Leaking bucket 为什么会延迟新请求？
q_en: Why can a leaking bucket delay new requests?
text: Leaking bucket 把请求放进 {{FIFO queue}}，再按固定 outflow rate 处理；突发流量会先填满队列。
text_en: A leaking bucket puts requests in a {{FIFO queue}} and drains at a fixed outflow rate; bursts fill the queue first.
why: 这能保护下游的稳定出流，但新来的请求可能排在旧突发后面。
why_en: It protects downstream steady throughput, but new requests can wait behind an earlier burst.

termDefinitions.meaning: FIFO：先进入队列的元素先处理。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: FIFO means the first queued item is processed first.

scenario: 服务 owner 修改了某类营销消息每天 5 条的限制，不希望重启所有限流节点。
scenario_en: A service owner changes the limit for a marketing-message type to five per day without restarting every limiter node.
q: 规则更新路径应怎么设计？
q_en: How should rule updates flow?
options: 规则库 + retriever 刷新
客户端代码写死限流规则
每次请求同步查询规则库
人工逐台机器改配置文件
options_en: Rule database plus retriever refresh
Hard-code rate limits in client code
Synchronously query the rule database each request
Manually edit config on every machine
why: 规则库是控制面，缓存是数据面；这样既能动态更新，又不会让每个请求都打到规则库。
why_en: A rule database plus cached refresh separates dynamic control-plane changes from the hot request path.
whenOtherWins: 如果规则永远不变且流量很小，静态配置会更简单。
tradeoff: 动态配置 vs 请求路径延迟
optionExplanations: owner 改完规则库，后台 retriever 负责刷新各节点的缓存，不用重启就能让新配额生效。
把规则写死在客户端代码里，每次调整配额都要发新版本，完全达不到不重启就能改的目标。
每次请求都同步查规则库会把控制面的延迟直接叠加到数据面，拖慢每一次限流判定。
人工逐机改配置文件既慢又容易漏改某台机器，规则在集群里会出现不一致的窗口。
optionExplanations_en: Once the owner updates the rule database, a background retriever refreshes each node's cache, so the new quota takes effect without a restart.
Hard-coding the rule in client code means shipping a new release for every quota change — the opposite of updating without a restart.
Querying the rule database on every request adds control-plane latency straight onto the hot path, slowing down every single decision.
Manually editing config machine by machine is slow and error-prone, leaving a window where nodes disagree on the rule.

scenario: 限流章节把入口限流类比为 TCP flow control：接收方先表达自己还能承受多少。
scenario_en: The rate-limiter lesson compares edge limiting to TCP flow control: the receiver advertises how much it can still handle.
q: Rate limiter 和 TCP flow control 的类比点是什么？
q_en: What is the analogy between rate limiting and TCP flow control?
text: 两者都不是盲目接收流量，而是根据接收方可承受能力给发送方一个 {{window 或 rate}} 边界。
text_en: Both avoid blindly accepting traffic by giving the sender a {{window or rate}} based on receiver capacity.
why: 这个类比提醒你：限流本质是在入口表达容量约束，不是后端被压垮后才补救。
why_en: The analogy is that both mechanisms express receiver capacity before the receiver is overwhelmed.

termDefinitions.meaning: TCP：面向连接的传输协议，包含流量控制等机制。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: TCP is a connection-oriented transport protocol with flow-control mechanisms.

q: Blob store 适合存什么数据？
q_en: What kind of data is a blob store built for?
text: Blob store 面向 {{unstructured data}}，例如图片、音频、视频和二进制文件，通常用扁平对象组织。
text_en: A blob store is built for {{unstructured data}} such as images, audio, video, and binaries in a flat object layout.
why: 它不靠表结构和 JOIN 表达关系，而是把大对象作为可寻址 blob 存取。
why_en: It stores large addressable objects rather than relational rows and joins.

scenario: 视频上传后很少原地修改，更新通常以新版本上传，旧版本仍可按保留策略存在。
scenario_en: Videos are rarely modified in place; updates are uploaded as new versions, while old versions may remain under retention rules.
q: 这种 WORM/immutable 假设带来什么设计简化？
q_en: What design simplification comes from a WORM or immutable assumption?
options: 写入后追加新版本，避免原地覆盖冲突
每次读都必须改写原始 blob
所有对象都必须放进关系型数据表
删除操作可以立刻同步擦掉所有副本
options_en: Updates append new versions, avoiding in-place overwrite conflicts
Every read must rewrite the original blob
All objects must go into a relational table
A delete can instantly erase every replica
why: 不可变对象让写路径更像创建新 blob 或新版本，避免大文件原地修改的一致性问题。
why_en: Immutable blobs turn updates into new versions, avoiding many in-place mutation consistency problems.

termDefinitions.meaning: WORM：写入一次、读取多次的访问模式。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: WORM means write once and read many times.

optionExplanations: 更新不再原地覆盖旧字节，而是追加成新版本，写路径不用处理并发原地修改的一致性问题。
读操作只是取字节，不该也不需要改写原 blob，这条说反了不可变假设带来的好处。
把所有对象塞进关系表放弃了 blob store 扁平对象组织的优势，跟这里的简化方向无关。
副本要跨节点异步删除，立刻同步擦掉所有副本忽略了删除传播需要的时间。
optionExplanations_en: Updates stop overwriting bytes in place and instead append a new version, so the write path avoids in-place mutation races.
A read just fetches bytes; it shouldn't need to rewrite the original blob at all — that's backwards from what immutability buys you.
Cramming every object into relational tables throws away the flat-object layout a blob store is built for, unrelated to this simplification.
Deleting a replica has to propagate across nodes; claiming it erases every copy synchronously and instantly ignores that propagation time.

q: 哪些场景天然适合 blob store？
q_en: Which use cases naturally fit a blob store?
options: 浏览器加载图片或文档
视频和音频流媒体
备份、归档、灾备
需要复杂事务 JOIN 的订单表
options_en: Serving images or documents to browsers
Video and audio streaming
Backups, archives, and disaster recovery
Order tables needing complex transactional joins
why: 这些场景都是大体积非结构化对象；事务 JOIN 更适合数据库而不是 blob store。
why_en: These workloads are large unstructured objects, while transactional joins belong in databases.
optionExplanations: 图片和文档是天然的非结构化二进制对象，按 blob 存取、按路径寻址正合适。
视频音频体积大且按顺序读取，适合切块存进 blob store 再做 range read 流式播放。
备份归档要长期低成本保留大文件，正是 blob store 分层存储擅长的场景。
订单这类需要跨表 JOIN 保证事务一致性的数据，更适合关系数据库而不是扁平对象存储。
optionExplanations_en: Images and documents are naturally unstructured binary objects, a good fit for flat blob storage addressed by path.
Video and audio are large and read sequentially, which suits chunking them into a blob store and streaming with range reads.
Backups and archives need cheap long-term retention of large files, exactly what a blob store's tiering is built for.
Data like orders that need cross-table joins for transactional consistency belongs in a relational database, not flat object storage.

scenario: 旧备份几乎不访问，但必须保留一年；热图片需要低延迟读取。
scenario_en: Old backups are rarely accessed but must be retained for a year, while hot images need low-latency reads.
q: 生命周期管理最应该做什么？
q_en: What should lifecycle management do?
options: 按访问频率分层，并按年龄过期清理
把所有对象永久放在最高性能层里
每天随机删除一批冷对象
禁止对象携带任何自定义 metadata
options_en: Tier objects by access frequency and expire by age
Keep every object in the top-performance tier forever
Randomly delete a batch of cold objects each day
Forbid objects from carrying any custom metadata
why: 冷热分层用读延迟和存储成本做取舍，过期规则负责清理不再需要的数据。
why_en: Tiering trades read latency for storage cost, and expiration rules remove data that no longer needs retention.
whenOtherWins: 如果所有对象都在毫秒级热读路径，统一热层会更简单。
tradeoff: 读取性能 vs 存储成本
optionExplanations: 旧备份冷但要留一年、图片热要低延迟，按访问频率分层加按年龄过期，正好把这两条需求分开满足。
所有对象都塞进最高性能层能满足图片的低延迟，但冷备份也一起付高成本，浪费存储预算。
每天随机删除冷对象既保证不了保留一年的要求，也可能误删还在保留期内的数据。
禁止对象带 metadata 会让访问频率、创建时间这些分层判据都无从获取，反而没法做生命周期管理。
optionExplanations_en: Since cold backups must last a year and hot images need low latency, tiering by access frequency plus age-based expiry satisfies both.
Keeping everything in the top-performance tier satisfies the image latency need, but cold backups pay the same high cost for no benefit.
Randomly deleting cold objects each day can't guarantee the one-year retention and risks erasing data still inside its retention window.
Forbidding metadata removes the very signals — access frequency, creation time — that tiering decisions depend on, breaking lifecycle management.

q: Blob store 的核心功能需求包括哪些？
q_en: Which are core functional requirements for a blob store?
options: 创建 container 并上传 blob
通过生成路径读取 blob
按保留期删除 blob 或 container
为每个 blob 执行跨表 SQL JOIN
options_en: Create containers and upload blobs
Read blobs through generated paths
Delete blobs or containers with retention behavior
Run cross-table SQL joins for every blob
why: Blob store 的 API 围绕 container、blob、路径和删除生命周期；JOIN 不是对象存储接口的主职责。
why_en: Blob-store APIs center on containers, blobs, paths, and lifecycle deletion, not relational joins.
optionExplanations: 创建 container 并上传 blob 是写路径的起点，account 下先建好容器才谈得上放对象。
通过生成的路径读取 blob 让读操作只认一个稳定标识，不用关心底层数据分布在哪。
按保留期删除 blob 或 container 让清理逻辑跟着生命周期走，而不是靠人工临时清盘。
对每个 blob 跑跨表 SQL JOIN 需要关系模型和查询优化器，不是对象存储接口该承担的职责。
optionExplanations_en: Creating a container and uploading a blob is where the write path starts — you need a container under the account before anything else.
Reading a blob through its generated path lets a read only care about one stable identifier, not where the data physically lives.
Deleting blobs or containers under a retention rule ties cleanup to the object lifecycle instead of ad hoc manual purges.
Running cross-table SQL joins per blob needs a relational model and query optimizer, which isn't what an object-storage API is for.

scenario: 估算一个 I/O 密集 blob 服务：峰值按 5M RPS 粗算，每台服务器保守按 500 RPS。
scenario_en: Estimate an I/O-heavy blob service with a rough 5M peak RPS and 500 RPS per server.
q: 服务器数量估算如何得到？
q_en: How do you estimate the server count?
text: 服务器数 = peak RPS / per-server RPS = 5,000,000 / 500 ≈ {{10,000 servers}}。
text_en: Server count = peak RPS / per-server RPS = 5,000,000 / 500 ≈ {{10,000 servers}}.
why: RPS = Requests Per Second，每秒请求数；这个数不是背答案，而是后续负载均衡、机房容量和监控阈值的输入。
why_en: RPS means requests per second, and this estimate feeds load balancing, capacity planning, and monitoring thresholds.

termDefinitions.meaning: RPS：每秒请求数，用来估算服务吞吐需求。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: RPS means requests per second and measures service throughput demand.

scenario: 每天 250,000 个上传，每个视频约 50 MB，缩略图约 20 KB，先按单副本、单清晰度估算。
scenario_en: There are 250,000 uploads per day; each video is about 50 MB with a 20 KB thumbnail, estimated as one copy and one resolution.
q: 每日新增存储量的粗估公式是什么？
q_en: What is the rough daily storage formula?
text: 每日存储 ≈ uploads/day × (video + thumbnail) = 250,000 × (50 MB + 20 KB) ≈ {{12.5 TB/day}}。
text_en: Daily storage ≈ uploads/day × (video + thumbnail) = 250,000 × (50 MB + 20 KB) ≈ {{12.5 TB/day}}.
why: 这个值只是单副本基线；复制、多分辨率和保留策略会把真实容量继续放大。
why_en: This is only the single-copy baseline; replicas, multiple resolutions, and retention increase the real footprint.

scenario: 同一 blob 服务每天新增约 12.5 TB，读路径按 5M DAU、每人 20 次、每次 50 MB 粗算。
scenario_en: The service adds about 12.5 TB per day; reads are estimated from 5M DAU, 20 reads per user, and 50 MB per read.
q: 为什么 outgoing bandwidth 会远高于 incoming bandwidth？
q_en: Why is outgoing bandwidth much higher than incoming bandwidth?
text: 写入带宽约 daily bytes / 86,400；读取带宽约 DAU × reads/user × object size / 86,400，因此读侧可到 {{hundreds of Gb/s}}。
text_en: Ingress is daily bytes / 86,400; egress is DAU × reads per user × object size / 86,400, so reads can reach {{hundreds of Gb/s}}.
why: DAU = Daily Active Users；读多写少会把 CDN、并行下载和缓存放到设计重点。
why_en: DAU means daily active users, and read-heavy bandwidth pushes the design toward CDN, caching, and parallel download.

termDefinitions.meaning: DAU：每日活跃用户数，常用来估算读请求和带宽。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: DAU means daily active users and is often used to estimate read traffic.

termDefinitions.meaning: CDN：把公开内容缓存到离用户更近的边缘节点。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A CDN caches public content at edge locations closer to users.

q: Blob store 的基础组件通常包括哪些？
q_en: Which building blocks commonly appear in a blob store?
options: Rate limiter 控制调用速率
Load balancer 分配请求
Metadata database 存对象元数据
Monitoring 跟踪磁盘和节点健康
options_en: A rate limiter controls request rates
A load balancer distributes requests
A metadata database stores object metadata
Monitoring tracks disk and node health
why: 这些组件分别保护入口、分摊流量、定位数据和触发扩容或修复。
why_en: These components protect the edge, spread traffic, locate data, and trigger scaling or repair.
optionExplanations: Rate limiter 挡在入口控制调用速率，防止突发流量或滥用直接压垮后端节点。
Load balancer 把请求分摊到多台 frontend 或 data node 上，避免单点扛下全部流量。
Metadata database 记录 blob 在哪些 chunk、哪些节点，是定位真实数据的入口。
Monitoring 持续跟踪磁盘和节点健康，故障发生时能触发扩容或修复流程。
optionExplanations_en: A rate limiter sits at the edge controlling call rate, stopping a burst or abuse from overwhelming backend nodes directly.
A load balancer spreads requests across multiple frontends or data nodes so no single one takes all the traffic.
A metadata database records which chunks and nodes hold a blob, acting as the lookup that locates the real data.
Monitoring continuously tracks disk and node health so a failure can trigger scaling or repair automatically.

q: Blob store API 为什么围绕 containerPath 和 blobPath？
q_en: Why do blob-store APIs revolve around containerPath and blobPath?
text: containerPath 通常包含 accountID + containerID；blobPath 再包含唯一 blob ID，让系统能 {{定位账户、容器和对象}}。
text_en: containerPath usually includes accountID plus containerID, and blobPath adds a unique blob ID so the system can {{locate account, container, and object}}.
why: 路径是 API 层的稳定名字，内部可以用 metadata 把它映射到 chunk 和 data node。
why_en: The path is the stable API name, while metadata maps it to chunks and data nodes internally.

scenario: 一个账号下可以有多个 container，container 不能嵌套，名字在同一账号内必须唯一。
scenario_en: An account can own multiple containers; containers are not nested, and names must be unique within the account.
q: 创建 container 时应检查什么不变量？
q_en: What invariant should createContainer enforce?
options: 同一 account 下 containerName 唯一
全世界所有账号不能用同一个 containerName
container 必须嵌套在另一个 container 里
每个账号只能有一个 blob
options_en: containerName is unique within the account
No two accounts globally can reuse a containerName
A container must be nested inside another container
Each account can have only one blob
why: 名字作用域在 storage account 内，过度做成全局唯一会增加协调成本且不符合 API 模型。
why_en: The name scope is the storage account, so global uniqueness would add unnecessary coordination.
whenOtherWins: 如果产品明确把 containerName 做成公开全局域名，才需要全局唯一。
tradeoff: 局部命名空间 vs 全局协调成本
optionExplanations: container 名字的作用域是账号内部，同一账号下不能重名就够了，不需要跨账号协调。
全世界所有账号都不能重名意味着每次创建都要跨账号做全局协调，成本远超实际需要。
题目已经说明 container 不能嵌套，要求它嵌套在另一个 container 里违反了这条约束。
一个账号能有多个 container，每个 container 也能装多个 blob，只能有一个 blob 与此矛盾。
optionExplanations_en: The container name only needs to be unique within its own account, no cross-account coordination required.
Requiring the name to be globally unique across every account means coordinating globally on every create, far more cost than needed.
The scenario already states containers cannot be nested, so requiring nesting directly contradicts that constraint.
One account can hold several containers, and each container can hold several blobs, contradicting a one-blob-per-account limit.

scenario: 同一 container 中用户再次上传同名 blob，系统假设 blob 不原地修改。
scenario_en: A user uploads a blob with the same name in the same container, and blobs are assumed not to be modified in place.
q: 系统应如何处理同名上传？
q_en: How should the system handle the duplicate-name upload?
options: 创建新版本或新唯一 ID
直接覆盖旧 chunk 且不记录版本
拒绝所有同名文件直到人工处理
把 container 删除后重建
options_en: Create a new version or unique ID
Overwrite old chunks without recording a version
Reject every duplicate name until manual handling
Delete and recreate the container
why: 版本化保留了不可变对象语义，也让并发同名写不会互相覆盖。
why_en: Versioning preserves immutable-object semantics and avoids overwriting concurrent uploads.
optionExplanations: 同名再次上传就生成新版本或新 ID，既保住不可变对象的语义，也让并发写不会互相覆盖。
直接覆盖旧 chunk 且不记录版本会破坏不可变假设，还可能让并发上传的两个版本互相踩掉。
拒绝所有同名文件直到人工处理会阻塞正常的重复上传场景，成本远高于自动生成新版本。
把 container 删除重建是极端操作，会连带清掉其它 blob，跟单个同名上传的场景不成比例。
optionExplanations_en: A same-name upload gets a new version or a new ID, preserving immutable-object semantics and keeping concurrent writes from clobbering each other.
Overwriting the old chunks without recording a version breaks the immutability assumption and lets two concurrent uploads stomp on each other.
Rejecting every duplicate name until manual handling blocks a perfectly normal re-upload scenario, far costlier than just versioning it.
Deleting and recreating the container is a drastic move that wipes out every other blob too, wildly disproportionate to one duplicate name.

scenario: 用户删除一个大视频，视频有多个 chunk 和副本；删除 API 需要低延迟返回。
scenario_en: A user deletes a large video with many chunks and replicas, and the delete API should return quickly.
q: 为什么先标记 DELETED 再异步 GC？
q_en: Why mark DELETED first and run garbage collection later?
options: 让用户立即不可见，同时避免同步删除所有副本的高延迟
确保删除请求永远不会成功
让旧数据继续可公开访问
把 metadata 和 data node 永久分离
options_en: Make it invisible immediately while avoiding synchronous deletion of every replica
Ensure delete requests never succeed
Keep old data publicly accessible
Permanently separate metadata from data nodes
why: 元数据标记先切断可见性，后台 GC 再慢慢回收 chunk；代价是空间回收会滞后。
why_en: A metadata tombstone hides the blob immediately, while background GC reclaims chunks later.

termDefinitions.meaning: GC：后台清理不再可达或已删除数据的过程。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Garbage collection is the background process that removes no-longer-reachable data.

optionExplanations: 先把 metadata 标记为 DELETED 让用户立刻看不到它，真正回收多个 chunk 副本的工作留给后台 GC 慢慢做，避免同步删除拖慢延迟。
标记删除后 API 立刻返回成功，删除请求本身是成功的，只是底层字节的回收还没完成。
标记为 DELETED 后前端查询就该把它当不存在处理，不应该让旧数据继续对外可见。
GC 只是清理已删除数据的后台流程，跟 metadata 和 data node 是否永久分离没有关系。
optionExplanations_en: Marking metadata DELETED first makes it invisible right away, while background GC slowly reclaims the many chunk replicas, avoiding a slow synchronous delete.
The delete API returns success right after the tombstone is set, so the request does succeed — only the byte reclamation is still pending.
Once marked DELETED, front-end lookups should treat it as gone; it shouldn't stay visible to the public afterward.
GC is just the background process reclaiming deleted data; it has nothing to do with whether metadata and data nodes are permanently separate systems.

q: Blob store 的高层架构链路是什么？
q_en: What is the high-level architecture flow of a blob store?
steps: Load balancer 把请求分发到 frontend servers
Client 发起上传、下载或删除 API
Frontend 与 manager 协调 metadata 和授权
Data nodes 存储或读取实际 chunks
Monitoring 观察节点和磁盘健康
why: 前端服务器处理 API，manager 负责位置和权限，data node 负责真实字节。
why_en: Frontend servers handle APIs, the manager handles placement and permissions, and data nodes store the bytes.
diagram:
flowchart LR
  C[Client] --> LB[Load balancer]
  LB --> FE[Frontend]
  FE --> M[Manager]
  M --> MD[(Metadata DB)]
  FE --> DN[Data nodes]
  MON[Monitoring] --> M
  MON --> DN

q: Blob 上传写路径应如何排序？
q_en: What is the correct order of the blob upload path?
steps: Manager 生成 blob ID 并选择 chunk 放置位置
Frontend 接收 uploadBlob 请求
Frontend 把 chunks 写到 data nodes
Manager 记录 blob metadata 和副本信息
客户端拿到 fully qualified blob path
why: 写路径先确定身份和放置，再写真实数据，最后把可寻址路径和元数据发布给客户端。
why_en: The write path chooses placement, writes chunks, records metadata, and then returns the stable blob path.
diagram:
sequenceDiagram
  participant C as Client
  participant F as Frontend
  participant M as Manager
  participant D as DataNodes
  C->>F: uploadBlob
  F->>M: ask placement
  M-->>F: blob id + chunk map
  F->>D: write chunks
  M->>M: record metadata
  F-->>C: blob path

q: Blob 下载读路径应如何排序？
q_en: What is the correct order of the blob download path?
steps: Manager 检查 public/private 权限
Frontend 用 blobPath 请求 metadata
Manager 返回 chunk 到 data node 的映射
Client 或 frontend 从 data nodes 读取 chunks
客户端缓存 chunk metadata 以便后续读
why: 读路径先拿 metadata 和授权，再按 chunk map 读数据；缓存 metadata 能减轻 manager 压力。
why_en: Reads fetch metadata and authorization first, then use the chunk map to read data and cache future lookups.
diagram:
sequenceDiagram
  participant C as Client
  participant F as Frontend
  participant M as Manager
  participant D as DataNodes
  C->>F: downloadBlob(path)
  F->>M: metadata + auth
  M-->>F: chunk map
  C->>D: read chunks
  C->>C: cache metadata

scenario: 下载 2 GB 视频时，metadata 只有 chunk 位置和权限信息，真实字节在 data nodes 上。
scenario_en: When downloading a 2 GB video, metadata contains chunk locations and access information, while bytes live on data nodes.
q: 为什么要分离 metadata path 和 blob data path？
q_en: Why separate the metadata path from the blob data path?
options: metadata 管位置，data node 传字节
所有视频字节都要经过 manager 转发
metadata 可以在读路径里直接丢弃
data nodes 只用来存账号名单
options_en: metadata handles location, data nodes carry the bytes
All video bytes must be relayed through the manager
metadata can be discarded directly on the read path
Data nodes only store the list of accounts
why: manager 擅长做位置和权限决策，不适合承载大文件传输带宽；字节流分散到 data nodes 才能横向扩展。
why_en: The manager should decide placement and authorization, while data nodes carry the scalable byte-transfer load.
whenOtherWins: 如果对象很小且吞吐低，让 frontend 代理数据会更简单。
tradeoff: 集中控制 metadata vs 分散传输带宽
optionExplanations: 下载 2GB 视频时，manager 只做位置和权限这类轻量决策，真正的大字节流走 data nodes，控制面和数据面分开才能横向扩展。
如果所有视频字节都经过 manager，2GB 这种大文件会直接把它的带宽和连接压垮，manager 撑不住这种流量。
metadata 记着 chunk 位置和权限，丢掉它读路径就定位不到数据在哪些 data node 上。
账号列表只是 metadata 里的一小部分，data nodes 存的是真实字节而不是账号信息。
optionExplanations_en: Downloading a 2 GB video means the manager only makes light location/permission decisions while the actual bytes flow through data nodes, so control and data planes can each scale on their own.
Routing every video byte through the manager would let a 2 GB file overwhelm its bandwidth and connections — it just isn't built for that traffic.
Metadata holds chunk locations and permissions; drop it and the read path has no way to find which data nodes hold the bytes.
Account lists are only a small slice of metadata; data nodes hold the real bytes, not account information.

scenario: Blob store 的 manager 维护数据节点、路径、权限和 chunk 映射；如果它挂掉，新请求会受影响。
scenario_en: The manager tracks data nodes, paths, permissions, and chunk mappings; if it fails, new requests are affected.
q: 如何降低 manager 单点故障风险？
q_en: How can you reduce the manager single-point-of-failure risk?
options: 定期 snapshot，standby 随时接管
metadata 只放在内存里不落盘
把权限检查这一步整个删掉
让客户端随机去猜 chunk 位置
options_en: Snapshot regularly so standby can take over anytime
Keep metadata only in memory, never persisted
Remove the authorization check step entirely
Let the client randomly guess the chunk location
why: snapshot 给 standby 一个可恢复的状态基线，故障后能从保存状态继续服务。
why_en: Persisted snapshots give a standby manager a recoverable state to take over after failure.
optionExplanations: 定期给 manager 状态打快照，standby 节点能从这份快照恢复并接管，故障后不用从零重建。
metadata 只放内存意味着 manager 一重启或崩溃，节点、路径、权限这些状态就全丢了。
删除权限检查解决不了单点故障，反而把访问控制这道保护也一起去掉了。
客户端随机猜 chunk 位置既没有恢复能力，也拿不到正确数据，不是可靠性方案。
optionExplanations_en: Periodically snapshotting the manager's state gives a standby a recoverable baseline, so it can take over after a failure without rebuilding from scratch.
Keeping metadata only in memory means one manager restart or crash wipes out every node, path, and permission record it held.
Removing authorization checks does nothing for single-point-of-failure risk and just strips away access control on top of it.
Having clients randomly guess chunk locations has no recovery story and won't even fetch the right data — it isn't a reliability plan.

q: Blob store 的 metadata 层级如何组织？
q_en: How is blob-store metadata organized?
text: 常见层级是 account → container → blob；blob metadata 再记录 {{chunk IDs, data node IDs, replica IDs}}。
text_en: A common hierarchy is account to container to blob; blob metadata records {{chunk IDs, data node IDs, and replica IDs}}.
why: 这个布局让 list containers、list blobs 和按 blob 定位 chunks 分别落在清晰的 metadata 层。
why_en: This layout separates listing accounts and containers from locating the chunks of one blob.

scenario: 用户上传 128 MB 文件，单个数据节点不一定连续持有整块空间，系统还要并行读取和复制。
scenario_en: A user uploads a 128 MB file; one data node may not have contiguous space, and the system wants parallel reads and replication.
q: 为什么把 blob 切成固定大小 chunks？
q_en: Why split blobs into fixed-size chunks?
options: 让大对象分布存储、复制和并行读取
让 metadata 完全消失
保证所有 chunk 永远在同一磁盘
让删除必须同步扫全盘
options_en: To distribute, replicate, and read large objects in parallel
To eliminate metadata entirely
To keep all chunks on the same disk forever
To force deletion to scan every disk synchronously
why: 固定 chunk 让 manager 可以计算 byte range，并把 chunk 映射到多个 data nodes 和副本。
why_en: Fixed chunks let the manager compute byte ranges and map pieces to data nodes and replicas.
whenOtherWins: 如果对象都很小，整对象存储能减少 metadata 和寻址开销。
tradeoff: 并行和容量弹性 vs metadata 数量
optionExplanations: 128MB 文件切成固定大小 chunk 后，各个 chunk 能分布到不同 data node、各自复制、并行读取，不必挤在一个节点上。
切成 chunk 反而需要 metadata 记录每个 chunk 落在哪个 data node，不是让 metadata 消失。
分布式存储的意义就是把 chunk 散到多个磁盘和节点，永远在同一磁盘违背了这个目的。
chunk 化让删除可以按 chunk 逐个异步回收，不需要同步扫描全盘去找数据。
optionExplanations_en: Splitting a 128 MB file into fixed-size chunks lets each chunk sit on a different data node, replicate independently, and be read in parallel instead of jamming onto one node.
Chunking actually needs metadata to record which data node each chunk landed on — it doesn't make metadata disappear.
The whole point of distributed storage is scattering chunks across many disks and nodes, so keeping them all on one disk defeats that purpose.
Chunking lets deletion reclaim chunks one at a time asynchronously, with no need to synchronously scan the whole disk.

scenario: 你在选择 blob chunk size：小 chunk 让调度更细，大 chunk 让 metadata 更少。
scenario_en: You are choosing blob chunk size: small chunks give finer placement, while large chunks reduce metadata.
q: chunk size 的主要取舍是什么？
q_en: What is the main chunk-size tradeoff?
options: 小增 metadata，大伤 I/O
小 chunk 不需要 metadata
大 chunk 提供强一致
chunk size 改用户名
options_en: Small adds metadata; large can hurt I/O
Small chunks need no metadata
Large chunks provide strong consistency
Chunk size changes usernames
why: chunk size 是 metadata 数量和数据面效率的折中，不能只追求越小或越大。
why_en: Chunk size balances metadata overhead against data-path efficiency, so neither extreme is automatically best.
whenOtherWins: 如果底层硬件和对象大小高度固定，按硬件块或对象分布定一个经验值即可。
tradeoff: metadata 开销 vs I/O 效率
optionExplanations: chunk 切得越小，需要记录的 chunk 数和 metadata 条目就越多；切得越大，单次 I/O 和迁移的代价就越重，两头都有成本。
不管 chunk 切多小，manager 都得记录它在哪个 data node 上，metadata 只会更多不会消失。
chunk 大小改变的是存储和 I/O 效率，跟一致性模型是不是强一致完全是两个维度。
chunk size 是存储层的参数，跟账户系统里的用户名毫无关系，这个说法文不对题。
optionExplanations_en: Smaller chunks mean more chunk entries and more metadata to track; larger chunks make each I/O and rebalance heavier — both directions carry a cost.
No matter how small a chunk gets, the manager still has to record which data node holds it — metadata only grows, it never disappears.
Chunk size affects storage and I/O efficiency; it has nothing to do with whether the consistency model is strong or not.
Chunk size is a storage-layer parameter and has no connection to usernames in the account system — this option is a non sequitur.

scenario: 用户经常 list 某个 container 下的 blobs；如果只按随机 blobID 分区，同一用户的数据会散在很多 partition。
scenario_en: Users often list blobs in one container; random blobID partitioning scatters one user's data across many partitions.
q: metadata partition key 更适合怎么选？
q_en: What metadata partition key is a better fit?
options: full path 范围分区
随机 blobID 打散
只按文件大小分区
只按上传 IP 分区
options_en: Range-partition by full path
Scatter by random blobID
Partition only by file size
Partition only by uploader IP
why: full path 让同账号同容器的数据更容易共置，list blobs 不用扫太多分区。
why_en: Full-path partitioning keeps related container metadata near each other, making list operations cheaper.
whenOtherWins: 如果唯一目标是均匀写入且几乎不 list，随机 blobID 分布会更简单。
tradeoff: 列表局部性 vs 写入均匀性
optionExplanations: 用户常常 list 一个 container 下的 blobs，按 full path 范围分区能把同账号同容器的数据放在相邻分区，list 不用跨太多分区扫描。
按随机 blobID 打散能让写入很均匀，但同一用户的数据会散落在很多分区，list 操作要扇出查询一大堆分区。
按文件大小分区解决的是冷热或容量分层问题，跟经常按 container 列出 blob 这个访问模式没关系。
按上传 IP 分区会让同一用户换了网络就换了分区，跟他实际访问的 container 结构完全对不上。
optionExplanations_en: Since users often list blobs in one container, range-partitioning by full path co-locates one account's container data, so a list scans few partitions.
Scattering by random blobID gives very even writes, but one user's data ends up spread across many partitions, forcing list to fan out widely.
Partitioning by file size addresses hot/cold tiering, not the access pattern of frequently listing blobs within a container.
Partitioning by uploader IP moves a user to a different partition the moment they switch networks, unrelated to their actual container structure.

scenario: 用户想按 upload date、media type 和 container name 搜索对象，并支持排序和分页。
scenario_en: Users want to search objects by upload date, media type, and container name, with sorting and pagination.
q: 应增加哪类能力？
q_en: What capability should be added?
options: tags + indexing engine
扫描所有 data node 字节
禁止用户 metadata
视频转成 SQL 行
options_en: Tags plus an indexing engine
Scan bytes on every data node
Forbid user metadata
Convert videos into SQL rows
why: 标签索引把搜索条件放在 metadata 层解决，避免每次查询扫描大对象字节。
why_en: Tag indexing answers searches in the metadata layer instead of scanning large object bytes.
whenOtherWins: 如果只按完整 blobPath 点查，不建二级索引也可以。
tradeoff: 搜索能力 vs 索引维护成本
optionExplanations: 按 upload date、media type、container name 搜索并排序分页，靠给 metadata 打 tag 加一个索引引擎在这一层就能查完，不用碰对象字节。
扫描所有 data node 上的字节意味着每次搜索都要读遍存储的大文件，代价高到不现实。
禁止用户 metadata 恰恰抹掉了这些字段可搜索的能力，比如上传时间、媒体类型这些查询条件根本没地方存。
把视频内容转成 SQL 行既做不到，也偏离了问题——要索引的是元数据字段，不是视频本身。
optionExplanations_en: Searching and paging by upload date, media type, and container name can be answered entirely at the metadata layer by tagging and indexing it, no need to touch object bytes.
Scanning bytes on every data node means reading through large stored files for every search — an unrealistically expensive approach.
Forbidding user metadata removes exactly the searchable fields like upload date and media type that the query needs, breaking search entirely.
Turning video content into SQL rows isn't feasible and misses the point — it's the metadata fields that need indexing, not the video itself.

q: List blobs 为什么使用 continuation token？
q_en: Why does listBlobs use a continuation token?
text: 当 prefix 匹配太多 blob 时，响应返回一页结果和 {{continuation token}}；客户端带 token 请求下一页。
text_en: When a prefix matches too many blobs, the response returns one page plus a {{continuation token}}, which the client sends for the next page.
why: token 让服务端保持稳定扫描位置，避免一次返回过大 payload 或用脆弱的页码偏移。
why_en: The token preserves scan position so the service avoids huge responses and fragile offset paging.

scenario: Blob store 要同时容忍磁盘/机架故障、同区域机房故障和整个区域故障。
scenario_en: The blob store must tolerate disk or rack failures, same-region data-center failures, and regional failures.
q: 副本应如何跨 failure domains 放置？
q_en: How should replicas be placed across failure domains?
options: 本地、同区域不同 DC、异区域分别放置副本
所有副本放在同一块盘上
只在客户端浏览器缓存一份
只保留 metadata，不复制 chunk
options_en: Place replicas locally, in another same-region DC, and in another region
Put every replica on the same disk
Keep the only replica in the browser cache
Replicate metadata only, not chunks
why: 副本要跨独立故障域才有意义；同盘副本不能抵御磁盘或机房故障。
why_en: Replicas must span independent failure domains; copies on the same disk do not protect against disk or site failure.
whenOtherWins: 如果只是临时缓存对象且可重算，同区域单副本也许能省成本。
tradeoff: 灾难恢复能力 vs 存储和复制成本
optionExplanations: 要同时扛住磁盘/机架、同区域机房和整个区域的故障，副本就得分别放本地、同区域另一个 DC、以及异区域，跨独立故障域才真正有用。
所有副本放在同一块盘上，磁盘一坏所有副本一起没了，连最基本的磁盘故障都扛不住。
只在客户端浏览器缓存一份既不是服务端可控的副本，用户清了缓存数据就彻底没了。
只复制 metadata 不复制 chunk，字节本身没有冗余，data node 一挂就真的丢数据了。
optionExplanations_en: To survive disk/rack, same-region DC, and full-region failures at once, replicas need to sit locally, in another DC in the region, and in another region — spanning independent failure domains is what actually protects you.
Putting every replica on the same disk means one disk failure wipes out all copies at once — it can't survive even the simplest failure.
Keeping the only copy in a browser cache isn't a server-controlled replica at all, and the data is gone the moment the user clears it.
Replicating only metadata and not the chunks leaves the actual bytes with no redundancy, so one data-node failure means real data loss.

scenario: 系统要求本集群内强一致和故障容忍，同时还要把数据复制到远端区域提高区域级可用性。
scenario_en: The system needs strong consistency and fault tolerance within the primary cluster, while also copying data to remote regions for regional availability.
q: 同步复制和异步远端复制应如何搭配？
q_en: How should synchronous and asynchronous replication be combined?
options: 集群内同步复制，远端 DC 异步复制
所有远端区域都同步阻塞写入
只异步复制 metadata 不复制数据
不做复制，只靠监控告警
options_en: Synchronously replicate within the cluster, and asynchronously replicate to remote DCs
Synchronously block writes on every remote region
Only replicate metadata asynchronously, not data
Do no replication and rely on alerts
why: 本地同步给写后读和故障容忍，远端异步避免跨区域 RTT 把上传路径拖慢。
why_en: Local synchronous replication protects strong reads and failures, while remote async replication avoids cross-region latency on uploads.
whenOtherWins: 如果业务要求跨区域 RPO=0，远端同步或共识复制才值得讨论。
tradeoff: 强一致写路径 vs 跨区域延迟

termDefinitions.meaning: DC：数据中心，包含机房内的计算、网络和存储资源。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A DC is a data center containing compute, network, and storage resources.

termDefinitions.meaning: RTT：请求到达对端再返回的往返时间。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: RTT is the round-trip time for a request to reach the peer and return.

termDefinitions.meaning: RPO：灾难发生时最多允许丢失的数据时间窗口。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: RPO is the maximum acceptable data-loss window after a disaster.

optionExplanations: 本集群内要强一致和容错，就同步复制拿到写后读保证；远端 DC 只求区域级可用性，就异步复制，不让跨区域 RTT 拖慢上传。
所有远端区域都同步阻塞写入意味着每次上传都要等最慢那个区域的 RTT 返回，延迟会被拉到很高。
只异步复制 metadata 不复制数据字节，等于目录还在但内容没备份，区域故障时数据本身仍然丢失。
完全不做复制、只靠监控告警，出问题时告警只能通知你数据已经丢了，挽救不回任何东西。
optionExplanations_en: Needing strong consistency and fault tolerance in the local cluster calls for synchronous replication there, while remote DCs only need regional availability, so async is fine and cross-region RTT never blocks the upload.
Synchronously blocking writes on every remote region means each upload has to wait for the slowest region's round trip, pushing latency way up.
Replicating only metadata asynchronously and not the data leaves the directory intact but the content unbacked up — a regional failure still loses the actual bytes.
Doing no replication and relying only on alerts means the alert can only tell you the data is already gone, with nothing left to recover.

scenario: Data node 磁盘故障后，该节点上的 chunk 副本不可读，系统需要恢复副本数。
scenario_en: A data-node disk fails, making chunk replicas on that node unreadable; the system must restore replica count.
q: heartbeat 和 re-replication 的闭环是什么？
q_en: What is the heartbeat and re-replication loop?
options: heartbeat 查坏节点，补齐缺失副本
客户端随机去读那块坏盘
只发告警，不更新路由 mapping
直接删掉 metadata 避免被读到
options_en: Heartbeat finds the bad node, missing replicas get copied back
The client randomly reads from that bad disk
Only alert, without updating the routing mapping
Delete the metadata outright to avoid it being read
why: 正常路径是心跳上报健康；故障后 manager 标记节点不可用、路由到健康副本，并复制新副本补回冗余。
why_en: Heartbeats detect unhealthy nodes, then the manager routes around them and re-replicates chunks to restore redundancy.

termDefinitions.meaning: heartbeat：节点周期性发送的健康信号，管理节点用它判断节点是否存活。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A heartbeat is a periodic health signal used to detect whether a node is alive.

optionExplanations: 节点定期发心跳，manager 靠心跳中断发现坏节点，把请求路由到健康副本，同时把缺失的副本复制回其它节点补齐冗余。
manager 发现坏节点后会把路由指向健康副本，不会让客户端继续去读已经确认故障的磁盘。
只告警不更新 chunk 到节点的映射，读请求还是会被指向那块坏盘，问题并没有被真正处理。
删掉 metadata 只会让这个 blob 彻底找不到，跟恢复副本数的目标背道而驰。
optionExplanations_en: Nodes send periodic heartbeats; when one stops, the manager marks the node down, routes to a healthy replica, and copies missing replicas elsewhere to restore redundancy.
Once the manager detects a bad node, it routes to a healthy replica instead — clients don't keep reading a disk already confirmed as failed.
Alerting without updating the chunk-to-node mapping still leaves reads pointed at the failed disk, so nothing actually gets fixed.
Deleting the metadata makes the blob unfindable entirely, the opposite of the goal of restoring its replica count.

q: Blob store 里哪些缓存层能分别减轻什么压力？
q_en: Which caching layers reduce which pressures in a blob store?
options: Client cache chunk metadata，减少重复问 manager
Frontend cache partition map，加快路由
Manager cache hot chunks，减少磁盘 I/O
CDN cache public blobs，减少 origin 读取
options_en: Client caches chunk metadata to reduce repeated manager lookups
Frontend caches partition maps for faster routing
Manager caches hot chunks to reduce disk I/O
CDN caches public blobs to reduce origin reads
why: 缓存不是一个点：metadata、routing、hot data 和公网分发各自挡住不同瓶颈。
why_en: Caching appears at several layers because metadata lookup, routing, hot data, and public delivery have different bottlenecks.

termDefinitions.meaning: CDN：把公开内容缓存到靠近用户的边缘节点。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A CDN caches public content at edge nodes close to users.

termDefinitions.meaning: I/O：系统读写磁盘、网络或设备的数据操作。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: I/O means input/output operations such as reading or writing disk or network data.

optionExplanations: Client 缓存 chunk metadata 后，同一批 chunk 不用每次都重新问 manager 要位置信息。
Frontend 缓存 partition map 能就近算出该转发到哪个分区，少一次跨节点查询再路由。
Manager 缓存热点 chunk 能直接命中内存，减少反复打磁盘 I/O 带来的延迟。
CDN 缓存公开 blob 让大部分读请求在边缘就返回，不用每次都回源打 origin。
